title: High performance workflows with Azure Logic Apps: using Azure SQL as storage provider.
summary: Azure Logic Apps can now use Azure SQL as a storage provider instead of Azure Storage for workflow state and runtime data, enabling better performance tuning, predictable costs, and enterprise-grade reliability features for standard logic app instances.
key_points: Azure Logic Apps traditionally use Azure Storage which can cause performance delays, especially in loops and connector actions
Azure SQL as a storage provider allows fine-tuning throughput and scaling based on workflow needs
Configuration requires enabling Azure services in SQL networking settings and selecting SQL storage type during Logic Apps creation
SQL acts as primary storage while Azure Storage remains as secondary for platform configuration hosting
Workflow state, run history, and runtime artifacts are stored in the SQL database in automatically created tables
features: Azure SQL storage provider for Logic Apps

quotes.text: you can now use Azure SQL as a storage provider instead of Azure Storage for your logic apps workflow related transactions.
quotes.why_it_matters: Introduces the new preview feature that addresses performance limitations of traditional Azure Storage approach

quotes.text: Possibility to fine-tune throughput and performance of workflows (you can scale SQL as per your needs)
quotes.why_it_matters: Key benefit showing how SQL enables better control over workflow performance characteristics
